subject: Archaeology
title: The Curse of the Pharaohs
description: Learn The Curse of the Pharaohs in one minute.

hook.text: When Lord Carnarvon died weeks after opening Tutankhamun's tomb, newspapers blamed an ancient curse.

buildup.text: Carnarvon died of an infected mosquito bite in April 1923. Reporters claimed lights went out in Cairo at the exact.

discovery.text: Howard Carter, who actually opened the tomb and spent years inside it, lived until 1939 — perfectly healthy at age 64.

twist.text: A study of 25 people present at the opening found they lived an average of 20 more years.

climax.text: Some scientists suggest toxic mold spores in sealed tombs could cause illness — a natural hazard.

punchline.text: The man who opened the tomb lived 16 more years.

quiz.question: What does statistical analysis show about the 'pharaoh's curse'?
options: People present at the tomb opening died significantly younger than average
The 25 people present lived an average of 20 more years — no curse effect
Only those who touched artifacts directly showed signs of illness
